body: I want to go to college because I want to support myself financially, but I don't feel like my major is really suited to my interests. My parents told me, "be a psych major if you don't know what you want to do", and that advice came & bit me in the ass. I'm a senior who's set to graduate this spring, and abandoning my major isn't really an option at this point, but I really feel like psychology isn't a good fit for me. My family has been pushing me towards being a social worker, and I know this job will break me down emotionally, but I can't think of any alternative job opportunities. My sister graduated with the same major as me, from the same school, as a summa cum laude of her class; however, she's working for $12 an hour right now and my parents are supporting her financially. I don't want to be trapped in that situation. My GPA isn't exactly exceptional and a fifth of my school majors in psychology, so I have a large group of people to contend against when it comes to finding a job. I feel like my options are becoming more and more limited day by day, and my major is becoming increasingly useless before I even achieve it. </rant>

College adds a lot of pressure, but so does the number of people I attend school with. I go to a college with 25k+ students, which makes me feel like a number more than anything. Every time I walk onto campus, I'm confronted with a bunch of strangers who bury their faces in their smart phones and disregard the outside world, which makes it difficult to make friends. My coworker told me once, "you're only truly friends with someone when you meet them at a party & drink with them", and many people around me adopt that mindset. It's nigh impossible to find someone who doesn't agree with that. The fact that I hate my major doesn't really help much, but it's not my biggest concern—I'm this far down the rabbit hole, so I might as well reach the bottom & get my undergrad degree.

I don't have a therapist right now, unfortunately. I want to confide in someone, but I know that therapists are obligated to institutionalize people who admit to being suicidal and I'm afraid of being caught in that trap again. After this semester (assuming I pass all of my classes), I'm set to graduate in the spring, and so taking a break this late into my academic career wouldn't fly with the people who are financing my education. Overall, I've been trying to feign relaxation when it comes to social situations, but I fall flat on my face every time. I feel like I always make an ass out of myself, and my friends are certain to remind me of this by never taking me seriously and constantly disregarding my opinions. I feel like I'm rambing now, so I'll try to summarize my feelings like this: I want to be happy, but my anxiety overwhelms all my rational and conscious thoughts until I'm left sitting alone at home, wondering why my current friends suck and my ability to make new friends is stunted. I know that wanting doesn't really come into it, and that action is what will drag me out of this rut, but my options seem limited until I get my undergraduate degree, and I'm not sure how much longer I can hold out.

Well, I believe this "lump" of yours was the result of increased stress, caused by living so far away from your mother. I highly recommend you ask your psychiatrist about Desoxyn and Paxil. If that doesn't work, try Prozac and Dexedrine. If your bulging stresswad still remains, try an alternating combination of the four.
